look: A city inside walls, packed with tall stone houses, baroque churches and palaces, with the spire of St Stephen's Cathedral above everything. Outside the walls lay a wide open strip, then the suburbs.
Men in knee breeches, long coats, three-cornered hats and powdered or tied-back hair. Women in long full gowns, with tall hairstyles and hats.
On foot, in sedan chairs carried by two men, in private carriages or in hired cabs called Fiaker.
Oil lamps on posts and house walls. Vienna had public street lamps from the late 1600s.
Mozart's opera The Magic Flute opened in a theatre just outside the walls in September 1791, and he died in Vienna that December.

stops.name: Vienna from the Belvedere palace
stops.title: Vienna seen from the Belvedere
stops.note: About 30 years before 1791, but the skyline barely changed in that time.

spots.d: The cathedral's south tower is 136 metres tall. It was finished in 1433 and was the city's landmark for centuries.
spots.how: It still stands at the heart of Vienna.

spots.d: The Belvedere gardens were laid out in the 1710s and 1720s for Prince Eugene of Savoy, a famous general.
spots.how: The gardens and both palaces can be visited today.

spots.d: Elegant visitors walk the paths in long coats, gowns and hats.
spots.how: Bellotto painted Vienna for the empress Maria Theresa, with great attention to detail.

stops.name: The Kohlmarkt
stops.title: The Kohlmarkt in Vienna
stops.note: A hand-coloured engraving made five years before 1791.

spots.d: The street's name means charcoal market. By the 1780s it was one of the smartest shopping streets, close to the emperor's palace.
spots.how: The Kohlmarkt is still a luxury shopping street.

spots.d: Shops filled the ground floors, with signs and awnings over the windows. Families lived on the floors above.
spots.how: Schütz drew the real buildings, many of which still stand.

spots.d: Coaches and cabs squeezed through narrow streets among people on foot.
spots.how: Vienna's hired cabs, the Fiaker, had run since the late 1600s.

spots.d: Men wore three-cornered hats, long coats and knee breeches. Women wore wide gowns.
spots.how: Fashion prints of the 1780s show the same style.

spots.d: The church that gave the square its name, once the parish of the imperial court.
spots.how: It still stands on the square.

spots.t: The palace and the court theatre
spots.d: The emperor's palace, the Hofburg, rose here, and beside it stood the court theatre, the Burgtheater. Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro had its first performance there in 1786.
spots.how: The old Burgtheater on this square was pulled down in 1888.

spots.d: Carriages brought nobles to the palace and the theatre.
spots.how: Schütz drew the traffic of the square as well as its buildings.

spots.d: A tall baroque fountain showing the wedding of Mary and Joseph, finished in 1732.
spots.how: It still stands in the square.

spots.d: A market since the Middle Ages. Under it lie the ruins of the Roman fort of Vindobona.
spots.how: Archaeologists found the Roman buildings beneath the square.

spots.d: Long coats, hats and full gowns, with children and dogs out in the square.
